topPRs.title: kona-engine: record the L1 origin of the local-safe head
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22528. Groundwork for the atomic snapshot query in #22527.

### Before

The engine's sync state held a local-safe head with no record of which L1 block it was derived from. To answer "which L1 block was the chain safe at, at this L2 timestamp?" — the query interop uses to decide cross-safety — a caller had to pair the head with a `derived_from` observed somewhere else, and the ChainController cannot do that reliably:

- The engine task queue is a `BinaryHeap` (`task_queue/core.rs`) and `EngineTask::Ord` returns `Ordering::Equal` for two `Consolidate` tasks, so among equal-priority consolidations the last `derived_from` forwarded is not guaranteed to be the last one executed.
- `Engine::drain` peeks, executes, and only then pops, so a task error halts the drain with that task still queued. A drain can end with local-safe written by an earlier task while later-forwarded origins were never consumed — pairing would then report an L1 key *ahead of* the head. `ChainController::step` drains at the top and enqueues at the bottom, so more than one consolidation really can be in flight.
- Two writers hold no L1 key at all: the derivation-delegation path, where the input is a bare `L2BlockInfo`, and engine resets, which install a walkback point found by traversing L2.

A wrong L1 key here is worse than no answer, since the caller has no way to tell the two apart.

### After

The pairing is recorded by the writer of the head, in the same step that writes it, and read back through one call:

- `EngineSyncState::local_safe()` returns the head and its origin from a single snapshot, so a consumer cannot observe a head from one update beside an origin from another. That is the read path #22527's handler needs; the handler itself is not in this PR.
- No writer can move the local-safe head without saying where it came from — the origin is part of the update, not a field beside it.
- Writers with no L1 key record an explicit "unpaired" rather than leaving a stale origin behind. A reset thereby *invalidates* the pairing it supersedes, instead of leaving one that describes a head the engine is no longer on.
- The absent case is a distinct variant, so a consumer cannot mistake it for a real L1 block the way a flattened `Option<BlockInfo>` defaulted to block 0 could.

### How

`LocalSafeOrigin` is `Unpaired | DerivedFrom(BlockInfo)`. `LocalSafeHead` bundles a head with its origin and is both the write shape — `EngineSyncStateUpdate::local_safe_head` becomes an `Option<LocalSafeHead>` — and the read shape.

`ConsolidateInput` derives the origin from its own variant: attributes supply their `derived_from`, a delegated `L2BlockInfo` is unpaired. `Engine::reset` / `reset_to` write unpaired. `InsertTask` trades `is_payload_local_safe: bool` for `local_safe_origin: Option<LocalSafeOrigin>`, carrying the same "is this local-safe at all" bit in its outer layer and the L1 key in its inner one; `SealTask` supplies it from the attributes it already holds, so nothing new is threaded through the build path. The Holocene deposits-only retry keeps the origin for free, since `as_deposits_only` copies `derived_from`.

Not in scope: #22528's rocksdb SafeDB store and #22527's query handler. Both issues stay open.


---

topPRs.title: kona-node-service: EngineActor becomes ChainController
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22527. Stacked on #22586.

**Before.** The actor that owns a chain's head state was called `EngineActor`, as if it wrapped the Engine API. Under interop a multi-chain host runs one of these per chain, so the name reads as one engine per chain. Separately, a gossiped payload at or below the local-safe head was inserted anyway, rewinding the unsafe head under a head derived from L1 and breaking `unsafe >= local-safe`.

**After.** It is the `ChainController`: the sole writer of the engine's heads, the mediator of every derivation-bound signal, and the owner of reset initiation. A gossiped payload is now admitted only if it descends from the local-safe head.

**How.** The rename covers the types that named the actor rather than the Engine API — `EngineActorRequest`, `EngineError`, `EngineRpcActor`/`EngineRpcRequest`, `EngineDerivationClient`, `EngineClientError`/`EngineClientResult`, and the `actors::engine` module. The last two also resolve a collision with kona-engine's own `EngineClientError`. `EngineConfig` keeps its name (it configures the real Engine API connection), as do the per-consumer `DerivationEngineClient` / `NetworkEngineClient` / `SequencerEngineClient` traits, which are named for their consumer. No wire names change: RPC methods, WS subscriptions and `dev_subscribe_engine_queue_size` are untouched, and the `engine` tracing target stays so operator log filters keep working.

The payload check rejects the two cases decidable from state on hand — a payload at or below the local-safe head, and one exactly above it whose parent is not that head — and admits anything further ahead, whose ancestry is not available and which derivation settles when local-safe catches up. Untrusted input is rejected rather than clamped: the payload is dropped at the queue boundary, next to the existing drop for an `INVALID` payload status. The check reads the state the write itself uses rather than the state at enqueue time, which the local-safe head can outrun; `EngineSyncState::apply_update` deliberately clamps only the cross-safe head, and this is what makes its assumption that no writer produces an unsafe head below it true for the one writer fed from outside the node.

**Not in this PR.** The issue also asks for a read-only query handler serving an atomic local-safe-at-timestamp plus L1-at-safe snapshot. That needs the L2 head paired with the L1 block it was derived from, and the pairing has to be recorded where the local-safe head is written, not inferred afterwards by the controller — a consolidation can fall back to build-and-seal and land a different block than the attributes named, so pairing "last `derived_from` forwarded" with "local-safe head after drain" can silently answer with an L1 key the head was not derived from. That makes it a `kona-engine` sync-state change, and it wants its own slice. Left as a follow-up on #22527; details in a comment there.

Two other items on the issue already hold from earlier slices in this stack and are unchanged here: the controller already mediates the derivation-bound signals and owns reset initiation, and the depth-1 lockstep confirmation is already fed from local-safe (with a lagging-cross test asserting it).

topPRs.title: op-reth: meter PostExec structural validation failures
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds a reason-labelled execution-client counter for PostExec block-level structural validation failures:

`optimism_post_exec.validation_failures{reason="..."}`

The bounded reason labels cover:

- `invalid_encoding_or_schema`
- `sdm_inactive`
- `multiple_transactions`
- `not_last`
- `block_number_mismatch`

The counter is recorded when op-reth rejects malformed PostExec structure while converting an Engine API payload, preparing block execution, or rebuilding derived payload attributes.

This addresses the observability question raised in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/388#discussion_r3829898758.

## Tests

- `cd rust && just fmt-check`
- `cd rust && cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-node --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cd rust && cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-node --lib`
- `cd rust && cargo check -p reth-optimism-evm --no-default-features`

## Review

The automated Rust review agent was unavailable in this harness; the change was manually reviewed against `docs/ai/rust-dev.md`.
